## ACCEPT — PM review (step 7)

### File surface vs declaration
Four files, exactly as declared:

| file | | |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` | modified | +119/−2 |
| `packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts` | modified | +74/−1 |
| `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.legacy-overlay-delete.test.ts` | added | +694 |
| `.changeset/legacy-overlay-delete-rolled-back-types.md` | added | +48 |

`packages/spec` read but never changed. **`packages/objectql` absent from the diff entirely**, which is the mechanical proof that ADR-0029 D9's pins were not edited — the constraint this card carried above all others. No `content/docs/releases/`, no `docs/adr/**`. Changeset present and `Check Changeset` green; `skip-changeset` correctly not applied, since this ships a real behaviour change.

### CI, per job
25 check runs, all `completed`: **23 `success`**, **2 `skipped`** (`Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate` — path-filtered). No failures. Named gates: `ESLint` success, `TypeScript Type Check` success, `Build Core` success, `Test Core` 3/3 + rollup success, `Dogfood Regression Gate` 3/3 + rollup success, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `ADR maintainer approval`, `No other open PR may claim the same issue` — all success.

### What I am accepting

**The tier boundary resolved into a registry-derived predicate rather than a hardcoded list, and that is the better answer.** I dispatched this with an enumeration (`permission` / `position` / `page` / `app` / `dataset` / `book`) and a standing instruction to STOP if the tiers could not be separated. They separate on the registry's own `supportsOverlay` flag — the types whose loader merges overlays at read are exactly the types where a stuck overlay is possible, and `object` declares `supportsOverlay: false`, so the carve-out cannot reach it structurally rather than by an exclusion someone has to remember. A hardcoded six-type list would have drifted the first time another type was rolled back.

**Both refusal points moved, which is what makes this a whole fix rather than half of one.** `deleteMetaItem`'s `environmentId` branch yields, and `SysMetadataRepository.delete` routes through the new `assertDeleteAllowed` carrying the same registry-derived rule — so the control-plane topology, which skips the first gate entirely because it has no `environmentId`, is released by the same rule rather than left refusing. That second path was the half most likely to be missed, and the pins cover both topologies.

**Create and update are verifiably untouched**: `put` still calls `assertAllowed` unchanged and `saveMetaItem`'s gates are not in the diff. The delete-only asymmetry is recorded in both gates' doc comments — including extending the save-side carve-out that promised "removing a row that predates this refusal is repair" to name the artifact-backed tier it never covered. That divergence between stated intent and enforced behaviour is what the card opened with, so closing it in the comment is part of the fix, not decoration.

### Reverse verification — the variant is what earns the ACCEPT

Reverted against the dev's own recorded base `f16e54e1d` (`git checkout <base> -- <2 source files>`, no `git stash`). Predicted 56 red, **measured 57 red / 44 passed**, with real output from both refusal points — project kernel `[not_overridable] … the type has not opted into per-org overlay writes` at `protocol.ts:11932`, control-plane `Failed to delete customization overlay: [NOT_OVERRIDABLE] 'permission' is not allowOrgOverride in the registry` at `:12152`.

**The variant verification is decisive and is exactly the damage case I required.** Relaxing the predicate for *every* artifact-backed type turned D9's own pin file to `2 failed | 14 passed` — precisely its two delete pins (`…and so is the RESET of one: deleteMetaItem answers NOT_OVERRIDABLE / 403`, and `a control-plane kernel refuses at the repository, and subtracts under the hatch`), plus 14 of this PR's own boundary guards. Variant reverted, D9's file back to 16/16. That proves the scoping is **necessary**, not merely sufficient — the over-broad fix is not hypothetical, it is measured, and it breaks exactly the two assertions the maintainer's D9 approval made binding.

**One missed prediction, reported rather than buried, and it found a second facet of the defect.** The guard "a delete with NO overlay row answers the no-op success instead of 403" went **red** on the project kernel, because the refusal ran *before* the probe for the row — so pre-fix, an artifact-backed item **with nothing customized at all** was refused too. The card described that ordering ("throws … before any probe for the row") without drawing out the consequence. Kept in the file with a corrected comment.

**Guards labelled as guards** (green in both directions, marked `[GUARD]` in the test names and the PR body): object-tier delete refusals on both topologies, every other `supportsOverlay: false` type, `put` still refusing `override-artifact` writes, `saveMetaItem` plain and org-scoped refusals, runtime-only delete still judged by `allowRuntimeCreate`. **Unmeasured: none.**

Suites all green with the consumption radius covered: `metadata-protocol` 1009, `objectql` 3066, `rest` 1278 (after clearing an AGENTS.md §9 unbuilt-dependency false red — correctly diagnosed as the stale-artefact trap rather than treated as a real failure), `runtime` 1906, `metadata` 593. Type-check debt measured at 63 and unchanged, zero in the new file.

### ⚠️ One scope note, stated so it can be vetoed cheaply

The delivered predicate also releases **`tool` and `skill`**, which my dispatch did not enumerate — they carry `supportsOverlay: true`, so they are the same registry shape and have the identical stuck-repair problem. I am accepting this as within the ruling: the maintainer's reasoning was general ("deleting an overlay restores the code-declared state; it is the narrowing direction and cannot widen anything"), and excluding two types that share the shape would leave the same defect alive for no reason. Flagging it explicitly because the ruling's text named the rolled-back six — if the intent was narrower, this is the line to object to, and it is one predicate to change.

### Filed, not fixed
**#7426** — `deleteMetaItem`'s catch re-wrap carries `status` forward but drops `code`, so a repository refusal reaches the caller as a 403 with `code: undefined` on the control-plane topology. That is not merely a new defect: it **explains** why D9's control-plane pin asserts a message substring while its project-kernel sibling asserts `code` + `status`. Correctly left out — fixing it changes the error envelope of every non-conflict failure on that path.

### Ruling
ACCEPT. Flipping out of draft, enabling auto-merge (SQUASH). Landing serialises behind the in-flight #4717 through the queue; the two are region-disjoint (`deleteMetaItem` + the repository gate here, `saveMetaItem`'s success return there).
